sources.description: OracleLoan.borrow(uint256) (src/OracleLoan.sol#33-41) uses a price feed answer without requiring it to be positive

plan.hypothesis: OracleLoan.borrow(uint256) uses the price feed's answer without checking that it is positive, so a non-positive answer (cast to uint256) becomes an enormous price.
plan.property: A feed that returns a non-positive answer must not let an account holding 1 wei of collateral take ETH that other users deposited.
preconditions: a victim has deposited SEED (10 ether) via deposit
the attacker holds 1 wei of collateral
the feed reports an invalid round (answer = -1) after having reported a healthy price

gates.detail: 3 slot values from the allowed vocabulary
attack phase uses no vm.store / etch / mockCall / deal(target) / ffi
pranks: attacker, attacker, attacker
asserts an attacker balance or owner change

fix.explanation: OracleLoan.borrow() reads the price feed and uses the answer as an unsigned price without checking it. A non-positive answer (an invalid round) is cast to an enormous uint256, which makes any account look massively over-collateralised. The patch rejects non-positive answers.
fix.change: require a positive oracle answer in OracleLoan

exploit.reason: Pramaan: oracle answer is not positive

verification.detail: exploit blocked (assertion-failed: Pramaan: oracle answer is not positive); 3 regression tests pass
